Convert new raw-unit data to the model's units

bl_apply_scaling.Rd

bl_set_scaling() is display-only: the model, the projection and every search work in the units the model was fitted on (for example z-scores), and functions that take new data – bl_select_target(), bl_project_points(), plot(..., target_point = ) – expect those units. bl_apply_scaling() applies the recorded transform standardised = (raw - center) / scale to new data given in original (raw) units, such as an external applicant, so it can be passed to them. It is the input-side counterpart of the raw-unit display.

Usage

bl_apply_scaling(data, bl_result)

Arguments

data

Data frame with every feature column in raw units. Other columns (e.g. class) are returned unchanged.

bl_result

A "bl_result", "bl_data" or "bl_filter_result" object carrying a scaling recorded by bl_set_scaling().

Value

data, with each feature column replaced by (raw - center) / scale.

See also

bl_set_scaling(), bl_select_target()

Examples

df       <- datasets::iris
df$class <- as.numeric(df$Species == "versicolor")
df$Species <- NULL
feats    <- setdiff(names(df), "class")
z        <- scale(df[, feats])
std      <- df
std[, feats] <- z
bl_dat   <- bl_wrap_data(std[1:100, ], std[101:150, ])
bl_dat   <- bl_set_scaling(bl_dat,
                           center = attr(z, "scaled:center"),
                           scale  = attr(z, "scaled:scale"))

# A new observation in raw units, converted to the model's units
new_obs <- df[1, feats]
bl_apply_scaling(new_obs, bl_dat)
#>   Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width
#> 1   -0.8976739    1.015602    -1.335752   -1.311052
all.equal(unlist(bl_apply_scaling(new_obs, bl_dat)), unlist(std[1, feats]))
#> [1] TRUE
